title: Latency Fingerprints & UX-Guided Dashboard Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to capture a compact taxonomy of latency "fingerprints" observed across inference requests, and an opinionated, UX-first set of dashboard widgets and trace anchors that help operators rapidly identify which fingerprint is active during incidents.

Why: 
We get many ‘latency’ incidents that are superficially similar but have different root causes (KV eviction vs network egress vs model fanout vs long tail queueing). The goal is to build a minimal set of signals + drilldown flows that map observable patterns -> likely cause -> next action. This should reduce mean-time-to-identify for oncall and reduce noisy alerts.

Quick definitions (fingerprints):
- Cold-start spike: sudden latency bump at model/container start; high P95/P99 with low throughput concurrently. Often accompanied by GPU / model load events.
- KV-warmth tail: stable median but fat P99-P999 due to cold KV entries or eviction storms. Characteristic: periodic long tails, often tenant-scoped.
- Multi-model fanout / routing burst: per-request CPU/GPU time spikes correlated with fanout_count > 1 or routing to heavyweight variants. Look for increase in model_switch_count and per-model latency differences.
- Network jitter (egress/ingress): increased client-RTT, increased TCP retransmits; affects both TTFB and overall response time. Network-level metrics (region, AZ) co-vary.
- Queueing / backpressure: latency across percentiles drifts up with increased inflight queue length and GPU utilization held near saturation. Slope from median->p99 grows with load.
- Tokenization overhead / long-context serialization: when tokenization or pre/post-processing dominates for small models; correlates with tokenization_time metric and request_input_size.

Minimal metric set to emit (instrumentation checklist):
- request.duration_ms (histogram+quantiles)
- request.step.{tokenize,encode,kv_lookup,model_infer,serialize}_ms (counters/histograms)
- kvcache.hits, kvcache.evictions, kvcache.latency_ms (per-tenant tag)
- model.load_events (timestamped start/complete) + model.variant (meta)
- routing.fanout_count, routing.model_switch_count
- infra.queue_length, infra.gpu_util_pct, infra.gpu_mem_free_mb
- network.client_rtt_ms, network.egress_bytes, network.p99_rtt_ms (region tagged)
- trace.sample_reason (canary/manual/auto) and trace.tags: tenant, route, model_id, request_id

Tracing conventions (proposal):
- Root span: request.id with attributes: tenant_id, route, input_tokens, model_id_hint, mode (sync/async)
- Standard child spans and attribute keys:
  - tokenize span: attribute tokenizer_version, input_bytes
  - kv_lookup span(s): kvcache_key_count, kvcache_hit=true/false, cold_read=true/false
  - model.load span: model_variant, binary_size_mb, load_reason (rollout/scale)
  - model.infer span: seq_len, generated_tokens, compute_device, gpu_kernel_tag
  - serialize span: output_bytes, format (json/stream)
- Sampling: aggressive adaptive sampling that prioritizes traces where request.duration_ms > P99 or where kvcache.evictions>0. For cold-starts, sample the first N requests after model.load_events.
- Trace annotation guideline: every span that interacts with external systems (KV, other model endpoints, network) must include remote_id and remote_latency_ms.

Dashboard/Widget proposals (compact set, prioritized):
1) Fingerprint Lens (top-left): a small stacked visualization that shows weighted contributors to recent latency incidents: Cold-starts / KV-tails / Fanout / Network / Queueing. Backed by quick rules (see mapping below).
2) Latency Portrait (center): percentile time-series (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) with overlay of throughput and GPU util. Allow slice-by drop-down (tenant, model, region).
3) KV Warmth Heatmap: tenant vs time heatmap showing kvcache.hit_rate and eviction_rate; quick links to traces for cells with low hit_rate + high p99.
4) Model Load Events timeline: vertical markers on latency graph; clicking a marker opens session of traces for first 2 minutes post-load.
5) Fanout Scatter: scatterplot of requests showing fanout_count vs latency; color by model_variant to spot heavy variants.
6) Network Region Blink: small KPI that flags region-level p99-client_rtt and packet-loss proxies; drilldown to infra network metrics.
7) Investigate Quickcards: pre-baked drilldown queries:
   - Cold-start quickcard: filter traces where model.load_events within last 120s and request.duration_ms > baseline -> show first 10 traces
   - KV-tail quickcard: filter requests with kvcache.evictions>0 or kvcache.hit_rate<0.6 and p99>threshold -> show exemplar traces with kv spans highlighted
   - Fanout quickcard: requests where routing.fanout_count>1 and p95>baseline -> list routes and counts

Mapping rules (how to classify an incident into a fingerprint):
- Cold-start: model.load_event present within 2 minutes + spike in p95 and p99 and low throughput and model.load_span durations > X ms.
- KV Warmth: kvcache.eviction_rate > 0.1 and p999 > baseline_multiplier * median AND kvcache.hit_rate < 0.8 for specific tenant.
- Fanout: routing.fanout_count median > 1.5 for affected requests and per-model latency variance high.
- Network: client_rtt p99 jumps correlated with region->egress metrics and no corresponding spike in model_infer time.
- Queueing: infra.queue_length increases concurrency correlated with linear increase in median and p95.

Alerting guidance (reduce noisy p99 alerts):
- Prefer fingerprinted alerts: rather than “p99 latency high”, emit “p99 latency high — KV-warmth fingerprint detected” with suggested runbook link.
- Use multi-criteria: only alert p99 if sustained > X for T minutes OR if queue_length>Y (to avoid short GPU jitter alerts).
- Deduplicate: if cold-start markers exist, suppress KV-tail alerts for the same window.

Owner / rollout plan (MVP):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): instrument missing spans (tokenize, kv_lookup, model_infer) + emit request.step.* metrics (owner: Marcus N.)
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): build Fingerprint Lens + Latency Portrait dashboard + quickcards (owner: Lena F.)
- Phase 2 (ongoing): adaptive trace sampler + alert routing by fingerprint + runbook pages (owner: Aisha P.)

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Sampling budget: how many traces per minute can we sustain at current retention? We need a small simulation (JIRA-OPS-741).
- Tenant tagging cardinality: adding tenant_id to every metric speeds root cause but increases cardinality cost — consider coarse bucketing for low-volume tenants.
- Fanout attribution: for requests that fan out to multiple model variants, we should record per-branch inference time to avoid blame shifting. Might need protocol change in runtime.

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Draft PR to add request.step.* spans + attributes (GH PR linked above).
- [ ] Sketch dashboard wireframe and get ops/product quick feedback (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Run a 48h trace-sampling smoke experiment on staging to validate adaptive sampler rules (owner: Omar).

Notes from last prod incident (2026-02-20):
- Incident manifested as periodic p999 spikes. Investigation found kvcache.evictions coincident with a churn in tenant X due to a bad sweep job. Our fingerprint rules flagged KV Warmth but we lacked a quickcard to jump straight to eviction traces. Adding that quickcard would have saved ~15m.

References and links:
- Tracing spec (working): https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tooling/pull/412
- Incident runbook draft: CONFLUENCE-OBS-289

Hand-off notes for SRE oncall:
- When an alert fires, open the Fingerprint Lens and check the top 2 contributors. If Cold-start is set, look at the Model Load Events timeline. If KV-tail shows up, jump to KV Warmth Heatmap and run the KV-tail quickcard. Default runbook pointers will be added to the alert payload (phase 2).

End of note — this is intentionally compact. Will expand into separate runbook + dashboard PRs once Phase 0 instrumentation lands.
